findings: At fixed winding and controlled external source current, subtracting external source work cancels the mutual magnetic energy. The resulting potential is (n-Phi_ext)^2/[2(Lg+Lk)], so outward force is I*Phi_ext_prime+I²*(Lg_prime+Lk_prime)/2.

Fixed wire volume gives a proportional to R^(-1/2), Lg_prime=log(8R/a)-1/2, and Lk_prime=2*kinetic_scale*R. The oracle includes the positive carrier kinetic stress; the completed shortcut omits only that contribution.
The same kinetic force follows from the centripetal acceleration of the fixed number of moving carriers: Nm*v²/R=Lk*I²/R. This agrees with the controlled-source energy derivative.

The reference uses complex virtual displacement of the full prescribed controlled-field London energy, independent of the explicit oracle force. Real finite differences and integrated mechanical work provide additional checks.

Current calibration depends on the same full fluxoid relation in both models and identifies the positive kinetic scale. The support-force sign, subtraction, fixed winding, material volume and external field are explicitly specified.

The public model now explicitly defines a uniform-current one-dimensional London approximation and claims only the supported thin-wire geometry a much smaller than R. It does not assert an unsupported penetration-depth limit. This qualification leaves the prescribed physical equations, calibration and grading unchanged.
